zh: the national saint of England. Many people believe he was a Christian martyr (= a person who is killed because of their religious beliefs) in the third century. According to the legend, he killed a dragon (= a fierce imaginary animal that can fly and breathe fire) to save a woman. He is often shown in pictures fighting the dragon.
en: the national saint of England. Many people believe he was a Christian martyr (= a person who is killed because of their religious beliefs) in the third century. According to the legend, he killed a dragon (= a fierce imaginary animal that can fly and breathe fire) to save a woman. He is often shown in pictures fighting the dragon.

zh: a red cross (+) on a white background, especially as a symbol of England and on the English flag
en: a red cross (+) on a white background, especially as a symbol of England and on the English flag

zh: 圣乔治节（4 月 23 日，纪念英格兰主保圣人的节日）
en: 23 April, the day of the national saint of England

zh: a small island in the southern Atlantic Ocean. It is famous as the place where Napoleon was kept as a prisoner by the British from 1815 until his death in 1821. It was owned by the British East India Company from 1659, and became a possession of the British Crown in 1834. The island's capital is Jamestown. The Governor of Saint Helena is also responsible for Tristan da Cunha and Ascension Island.
en: a small island in the southern Atlantic Ocean. It is famous as the place where Napoleon was kept as a prisoner by the British from 1815 until his death in 1821. It was owned by the British East India Company from 1659, and became a possession of the British Crown in 1834. The island's capital is Jamestown. The Governor of Saint Helena is also responsible for Tristan da Cunha and Ascension Island.

zh: 圣赫利尔（海峡群岛中泽西岛的首府）
en: the capital of Jersey, in the Channel Islands

zh: a town on the coast of Cornwall in south-west England. It is popular with tourists, and several well-known artists have lived there, including Bernard Leach (1887-1979), Barbara Hepworth, Ben Nicholson and Patrick Heron (1920-99). A branch of Tate Britain opened in St Ives in 1993. The town is also mentioned in a traditional nursery rhyme which contains a riddle to which the answer is one, since the man and his wives, etc. were going the other way: “As I was going to St Ives,I met a man with seven wives.Each wife had seven sacks,Each sack had seven cats,Each cat had seven kits;Kits, cats, sacks and wives,How many were going to Saint Ives?”
en: a town on the coast of Cornwall in south-west England. It is popular with tourists, and several well-known artists have lived there, including Bernard Leach (1887-1979), Barbara Hepworth, Ben Nicholson and Patrick Heron (1920-99). A branch of Tate Britain opened in St Ives in 1993. The town is also mentioned in a traditional nursery rhyme which contains a riddle to which the answer is one, since the man and his wives, etc. were going the other way: “As I was going to St Ives,I met a man with seven wives.Each wife had seven sacks,Each sack had seven cats,Each cat had seven kits;Kits, cats, sacks and wives,How many were going to Saint Ives?”

zh: a large, grand house built by King Henry VIII in 1552 at the edge of St James's Park in London. It was the main London home of the king or queen from 1697 to 1837.
en: a large, grand house built by King Henry VIII in 1552 at the edge of St James's Park in London. It was the main London home of the king or queen from 1697 to 1837.

zh: a park in central London, in front of Buckingham Palace. It is the oldest of London's royal parks, and contains a long lake with an island where many birds breed.
en: a park in central London, in front of Buckingham Palace. It is the oldest of London's royal parks, and contains a long lake with an island where many birds breed.

zh: a British charity that was founded in 1887. Its staff work without payment to provide medical care at public events, such as concerts or football matches. They also run medical centres and services for people with no homes, and provide training in first aid. The charity is named after the Order of the Hospital of St John of Jerusalem, an ancient military organization that cared for the sick.
en: a British charity that was founded in 1887. Its staff work without payment to provide medical care at public events, such as concerts or football matches. They also run medical centres and services for people with no homes, and provide training in first aid. The charity is named after the Order of the Hospital of St John of Jerusalem, an ancient military organization that cared for the sick.

zh: 圣约翰斯（加拿大纽芬兰和拉布拉多省首府，纽芬兰岛东南沿海港口）
en: the capital city of the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador, a port on the south-eastern coast of the island of Newfoundland

zh: 金丝桃，圣约翰草（可入药）
en: a herb with yellow flowers, used in medicines

zh: (1st century AD) a rich supporter of Jesus who appears in the Bible. He asks for Jesus's body after he dies and puts it in his own tomb. In traditional English stories he is said to have visited Glastonbury in Somerset, bringing the Holy Grail with him, and to have started the first English church. A thorn tree at Glastonbury is said to have grown from the stick that he carried.
en: (1st century AD) a rich supporter of Jesus who appears in the Bible. He asks for Jesus's body after he dies and puts it in his own tomb. In traditional English stories he is said to have visited Glastonbury in Somerset, bringing the Holy Grail with him, and to have started the first English church. A thorn tree at Glastonbury is said to have grown from the stick that he carried.

zh: a group of four islands off the west coast of Scotland, at the most western point in Britain. Nobody has lived there since 1930. The islands' high mountains and cliffs are the home of many different sea birds. St Kilda became a World Heritage Site in 1986.
en: a group of four islands off the west coast of Scotland, at the most western point in Britain. Nobody has lived there since 1930. The islands' high mountains and cliffs are the home of many different sea birds. St Kilda became a World Heritage Site in 1986.

zh: 圣基茨和尼维斯（由两个岛屿组成的加勒比海国家）
en: a country consisting of two islands in the eastern Caribbean Sea. It was claimed by Britain in 1623, and the island of Anguilla was part of it until 1967. In 1983 it became an independent member of the Commonwealth. Its capital town is Basseterre.

zh: a major water transport system for the US and Canada. It was built by the two countries and opened in 1959. It connects the St Lawrence River with Lake Ontario and then, with the Great Lakes system, forms a channel 2 342 miles/3 768 kilometres long. Large ships use it to travel between the Atlantic Ocean and the Great Lakes.
en: a major water transport system for the US and Canada. It was built by the two countries and opened in 1959. It connects the St Lawrence River with Lake Ontario and then, with the Great Lakes system, forms a channel 2 342 miles/3 768 kilometres long. Large ships use it to travel between the Atlantic Ocean and the Great Lakes.

zh: 圣路易斯（美国密苏里州密西西比河沿岸城市）
en: a city on the Mississippi River in the US state of Missouri. It was established in 1764 by the French, who named it after King Louis IX. It was part of the Louisiana Purchase and became a major port for steamboats (= river boats driven by steam) in the 19th century. It now produces cars, aircraft, metal and chemicals. The city was known as the 'Gateway to the West', and its Gateway Arch (630 feet/192 metres high) is a symbol of this.

zh: 圣卢西亚（加勒比海岛国）
en: an island in the Caribbean Sea. It was claimed by Britain in 1814 and has been an independent member of the Commonwealth since 1979. Its capital town is Castries.

zh: 圣卢西亚人；圣卢西亚的；圣卢西亚人的
en: (a person) from St Lucia

zh: a church in central London, designed by James Gibbs and completed in 1726. The Academy of St Martin-in-the-Fields was originally based there, and performances by other musical groups are still given there. The church also started an art college in 1854, now called the Central St Martin's College of Art and Design in Bloomsbury.
en: a church in central London, designed by James Gibbs and completed in 1726. The Academy of St Martin-in-the-Fields was originally based there, and performances by other musical groups are still given there. The church also started an art college in 1854, now called the Central St Martin's College of Art and Design in Bloomsbury.

zh: a large train station in central London, for trains to and from the Midlands. The station building was designed in a Gothic style by George Gilbert Scott and opened in 1868. St Pancras also has a London Underground station which it shares with King's Cross. Since 2007 St Pancras has been a terminus for trains using the Channel Tunnel.
en: a large train station in central London, for trains to and from the Midlands. The station building was designed in a Gothic style by George Gilbert Scott and opened in 1868. St Pancras also has a London Underground station which it shares with King's Cross. Since 2007 St Pancras has been a terminus for trains using the Channel Tunnel.

zh: (c. 389-c. 461) the national saint of Ireland. He was probably born in Wales, the son of a Roman father. Patrick became a monk in Gaul (= France) and went to Ireland in 432. He converted many people to Christianity, and there are many stories about his great powers, including one which explains why there are no snakes in Ireland. Patrick is said to have tricked them all so that they went into the sea and drowned. He is also said to have used the shamrock plant to explain the Christian idea of the Trinity, because it has three leaves on one stem. That is why it is traditional for Irish people to wear a shamrock on St Patrick's Day, 17 March.
en: (c. 389-c. 461) the national saint of Ireland. He was probably born in Wales, the son of a Roman father. Patrick became a monk in Gaul (= France) and went to Ireland in 432. He converted many people to Christianity, and there are many stories about his great powers, including one which explains why there are no snakes in Ireland. Patrick is said to have tricked them all so that they went into the sea and drowned. He is also said to have used the shamrock plant to explain the Christian idea of the Trinity, because it has three leaves on one stem. That is why it is traditional for Irish people to wear a shamrock on St Patrick's Day, 17 March.

zh: the largest Roman Catholic church in the US, on Fifth Avenue, New York. It was designed by James Renwick (1818-95) in a mixture of French and English Gothic styles, and completed in 1879.
en: the largest Roman Catholic church in the US, on Fifth Avenue, New York. It was designed by James Renwick (1818-95) in a mixture of French and English Gothic styles, and completed in 1879.

zh: 圣帕特里克节（3 月 17 日，纪念爱尔兰的主保圣人圣帕特里克的基督教节日，很多爱尔兰人佩戴三叶草）
en: 17 March, a Christian festival of the national saint of Ireland, when many Irish people wear a shamrock

zh: 圣保罗（美国明尼苏达州首府，位于密西西比河沿岸。圣保罗和明尼阿波利斯被称作“双子市”）
en: the capital city of the US state of Minnesota. It is on the Mississippi River which separates it from Minneapolis, and the two are known as the 'Twin Cities'. St Paul was first established in 1840, when it was called Pig's Eye Landing. It became the capital of the Minnesota Territory in 1849. Today it produces computers and other electronic equipment and cars. It has a famous Winter Carnival each year.

zh: a large cathedral in London. It was designed in the late 17th century by Sir Christopher Wren to replace a previous cathedral destroyed in the Fire of London, and was completed in 1710. It has a large dome (= a round roof with a circular base), inside which is the famous Whispering Gallery. The cathedral contains the graves of many famous people, including Lord Nelson, the Duke of Wellington and Christopher Wren himself.“Si monumentum requiris, circumspice. (If you seek a monument, look around you.)”words carved in St Paul's Cathedral with reference to Christopher Wren
en: a large cathedral in London. It was designed in the late 17th century by Sir Christopher Wren to replace a previous cathedral destroyed in the Fire of London, and was completed in 1710. It has a large dome (= a round roof with a circular base), inside which is the famous Whispering Gallery. The cathedral contains the graves of many famous people, including Lord Nelson, the Duke of Wellington and Christopher Wren himself.“Si monumentum requiris, circumspice. zh: 圣彼得港（海峡群岛中根西岛的首府）
en: the capital of Guernsey, in the Channel Islands

zh: 圣斯威辛瞻礼日（7 月 15 日，基督教节日，在英国据说如该日下雨则将持续下雨四十天）
en: 15 July, a Christian festival. In the UK it is said that if it rains on this day it will rain for the next forty days.

zh: (c. 1118-70) an English saint. He was a close friend of King Henry II, who made him chancellor (= senior law official) and later Archbishop of Canterbury, hoping by doing this to be able to control the English Church. When Thomas resisted they argued. According to tradition, Henry said, ‘Who will rid me of this turbulent priest?’ As a result four knights murdered Becket in Canterbury Cathedral, which became a place of pilgrimage where people travelled to show respect for the saint. His story was made into a play, Murder in the Cathedral (1935), by T S Eliot.
en: (c. 1118-70) an English saint. He was a close friend of King Henry II, who made him chancellor (= senior law official) and later Archbishop of Canterbury, hoping by doing this to be able to control the English Church. When Thomas resisted they argued. According to tradition, Henry said, ‘Who will rid me of this turbulent priest?’ As a result four knights murdered Becket in Canterbury Cathedral, which became a place of pilgrimage where people travelled to show respect for the saint. His story was made into a play, Murder in the Cathedral (1935), by T S Eliot.

zh: a large teaching hospital in central London, established in the early 12th century and later named after St Thomas Becket. It moved to its present buildings opposite the Houses of Parliament in 1871. Since 1993 it has been managed as part of a hospital trust with Guy's Hospital and King's College Hospital.
en: a large teaching hospital in central London, established in the early 12th century and later named after St Thomas Becket. It moved to its present buildings opposite the Houses of Parliament in 1871. Since 1993 it has been managed as part of a hospital trust with Guy's Hospital and King's College Hospital.

zh: an imaginary public school for girls in the humorous drawings of Ronald Searle. The girls are famous for their bad behaviour, and have appeared in several books and films, e.g. The Belles of Saint Trinian's (1954).
en: an imaginary public school for girls in the humorous drawings of Ronald Searle. The girls are famous for their bad behaviour, and have appeared in several books and films, e.g. The Belles of Saint Trinian's (1954).

zh: 圣瓦伦丁节，情人节（2 月 14 日，人们常以匿名形式送情人卡）

zh: 圣文森特和格林纳丁斯（加勒比海的群岛国家）
en: a country consisting of a group of islands in the Caribbean Sea. It was claimed by Britain in 1783 and became an independent member of the Commonwealth in 1979. Its capital town is Kingstown.

zh: Sydenham’s chorea (= a disease that mostly affects children, which causes the body to make small sudden movements and often follows rheumatic fever)
en: Sydenham’s chorea (= a disease that mostly affects children, which causes the body to make small sudden movements and often follows rheumatic fever)

ex: He was stabbed to death in a racist attack.
他遭到种族主义者的袭击，被刺死了。

zh: 持刀（或其他利器）伤人事件

ex: a fatal stabbing
持刀伤人致死事件

zh: 稳定（性）；稳固（性）

ex: political/economic/social stability
政治／经济／社会稳定

zh: 健身球
en: a large ball that you can sit on when doing exercises to make your muscles work in a different way

经济稳定性

zh: （使）稳定，稳固

患者的病情稳定下来。

zh: 稳定装置；（航空器的）安定面；（船舶的）减摇装置
（儿童自行车后轮两侧的）稳定轮
稳定剂

ex: She can ride her bike without stabilizers now.
她现在可以不用稳定器骑自行车了。

稳重的；沉稳的；持重的
（化学状态或原子状态）稳定的

ex: The patient's condition is stable (= it is not getting worse).
患者病情稳定。

zh: 饲养马的人；马倌；马夫

zh: 同机构的人（或产品）；同事；同伙

while staying in the same state; without changing in unexpected ways

en: a first name for girls

en: a pile of something, usually neatly arranged

一摞书

（与其他人或事物）相比；比得上
看来合理；讲得通；合乎情理

公共汽车后面的汽车很快排成了长龙。

摆满了玻璃杯的桌子

zh: 参谋

zh: 陆军上士；（美国）空军中士

陆军上士鲍勃 · 伍兹

en: a person whose job is to write stories, articles, etc. for a newspaper, magazine, radio or television company. A staff writer is employed by one particular organization and works in one of their offices.
ex: She's a staff writer on a popular show.
她是一个受欢迎的节目的幕后作家。

zh: an island in the Hebrides, Scotland, close to Mull. Nobody lives there but many people visit the island to see Fingal's Cave and the rocks there, which are well known for their unusual shapes.

zh: (1889-1952) a British labour politician who is best remembered for his policy of ' austerity' after World War Two, when as Chancellor of the Exchequer he kept a tight control over Britain's economy. He was the nephew of Beatrice Webb, and was made a knight in 1930.
en: (1889-1952) a British labour politician who is best remembered for his policy of ' austerity' after World War Two, when as Chancellor of the Exchequer he kept a tight control over Britain's economy. He was the nephew of Beatrice Webb, and was made a knight in 1930.

zh: a small, strong breed of dog. It was originally bred in Staffordshire for dog fights (= events in which two dogs fight and people bet on which one will win) and for bull-baiting (= using dogs to annoy a bull) in the early 19th century. In the 1980s it was fashionable in Britain to have these dogs as pets, particularly among people in cities who wanted to appear strong or dangerous. In the 1990s more people bought them after a new law made it difficult to own the larger and more violent American pit bull terriers.

zh: a pottery figure made in Staffordshire from the 18th century and after. Many people like to collect the small painted models of animals and people, often of famous or historical figures, and they are often used in people's homes for decoration.
en: a pottery figure made in Staffordshire from the 18th century and after. Many people like to collect the small painted models of animals and people, often of famous or historical figures, and they are often used in people's homes for decoration.

zh: 雄鹿

男子婚前聚会（只招待男性朋友）
en: the night before a man’s wedding, often spent with his male friends

zh: （发展或进展的）时期，阶段，状态

（多指剧场中的）舞台
戏剧；戏剧表演；戏剧界

我目前无法做出决定。

ex: The stage direction reads, ‘Exit left’.
舞台方向显示为“向左退出”。

zh: 剧场后门（供演职人员进出）

ex: A crowd of fans was waiting outside the stage door.
一群歌迷在舞台门外等着。

zh: 怯场（演员出场前的紧张不安）
en: nervous feelings felt by performers before they appear in front of an audience
ex: Even experienced actors can suffer from stage fright.
即使富有经验的演员也会怯场。

zh: （演员面对观众时的）舞台左侧
en: on the left side of a stage in a theatre, as seen by an actor facing the audience

zh: 舞台监督
en: the person who is responsible for the stage, lights, scenery, etc. during the performance of a play in a theatre

zh: （演员的）艺名
en: a name that an actor uses instead of his or her real name
ex: David Harries adopted the stage name Dixon Hare when he became a full-time actor.
戴维·哈里斯成为专职演员后用了狄克逊·黑尔作为艺名。

zh: （演员面对观众时的）舞台右侧
en: on the right side of a stage in a theatre, as seen by an actor facing the audience

zh: 低声旁白（演员避开台上其他角色说给观众听的）

“我早知道会出这样的事。” 她轻声说给所有人听。

zh: 担任舞台监督

ex: The entire sequence of events was stage-managed by the government.
整个事件序列由政府进行阶段管理。

zh: 醉心舞台渴望当演员的
en: enjoying the theatre a lot and wishing very much to become an actor

zh: （旧时的）驿站马车，公共马车
en: a large carriage pulled by horses that was used in the past to carry passengers, and often mail, along a regular route
ex: Stagecoaches were often attacked by robbers and bandits.
驿马车经常遭到强盗和土匪的袭击。

zh: 舞台表演技巧；剧场表演艺术
en: skill in presenting plays in a theatre

zh: 舞台工作人员（负责移动布景、准备道具等）
en: a person whose job is to help move scenery, etc. in a theatre, to prepare the stage for the next play or the next part of a play

zh: a party held for a woman who will soon get married, attended only by women
en: a party held for a woman who will soon get married, attended only by women
ex: His fiancée had gone to a bar in town for her stagette.
他的未婚妻去城里的一家酒吧上舞台。

zh: 不自然的；做作的；演戏似的
en: not natural, as if it is being acted by somebody in a play

zh: 滞胀（高通胀与低就业率或经济低迷并存）
en: an economic situation where there is high inflation (= prices rising continuously) but no increase in the jobs that are available or in business activity

zh: 摇摇晃晃地走；蹒跚；踉跄
en: a weak unsteady way of walking, as if you are about to fall
ex: to walk with a stagger
蹒跚着走

zh: 震惊；大吃一惊
交错的；错开的
en: very surprised and shocked at something you are told or at something that happens
ex: I was staggered at the amount of money the ring cost.
那戒指那么贵，我非常吃惊。

zh: 令人难以相信的
en: so great, shocking or surprising that it is difficult to believe
ex: They paid a staggering £5 million for the house.
他们为这所房子花了惊人的500万英镑。

zh: 令人难以相信的
en: in a way that is so great, shocking or surprising that it is difficult to believe
ex: staggeringly beautiful/expensive
漂亮／昂贵得令人难以置信

zh: 演出形式；演出风格
临时工作台（或工作架）
en: the way in which a play is produced and presented on stage
ex: a modern staging of ‘King Lear’
以现代风格演出的《李尔王》

zh: an area where soldiers and equipment are gathered before a military operation
a place where people gather to organize an activity or a trip
en: an area where soldiers and equipment are gathered before a military operation
ex: a staging area for training exercises
训练练习的暂存区

zh: 中途站（或机场、停靠码头）
en: a place where people, planes, ships, etc. regularly stop during a long journey

zh: （水或空气）不流动而污浊的
停滞的；不发展的；无变化的
en: stagnant water or air is not moving and therefore smells unpleasant
ex: Few fish survive in the stagnant waters of the lake.
在停滞的湖水中很少有鱼类生存。

zh: 停滞；不发展；不进步
因不流动而变得污浊
en: to stop developing or making progress
ex: Profits have stagnated.
利润原地踏步。

zh: 停滞；不发展；不进步
（水或空气）不流动而污浊的
en: the fact of no longer developing or making progress
ex: a period of economic stagnation
经济停滞时期

zh: 不自然的；做作的；演戏似的
en: not natural, as if it is being acted by somebody in a play
ex: He fell to the ground writhing in stagy agony.
他陷入沉闷的痛苦中摔倒在地。

zh: 没意思的；古板的；一本正经的
en: not fun or interesting; boring and old-fashioned
ex: The museum is trying to get rid of its staid image.
这家博物馆正努力摆脱古板的形象。

zh: （被）玷污；留下污渍
给…染色（或着色）
玷污，败坏（名声）
en: to leave a mark that is difficult to remove on something; to be marked in this way
ex: I hope it doesn't stain the carpet.
希望它别把地毯弄脏。

zh: 满是污痕的；沾有污渍的
en: covered with stains or marked with a stain
ex: My dress was stained.
我的连衣裙弄上了污渍。

zh: 彩色玻璃
en: pieces of coloured glass that are put together to make windows showing pictures or special designs, especially in churches

zh: 不锈钢
en: a type of steel that does not rust (= change colour)
ex: knives made of stainless steel
不锈钢刀具

zh: 梯级
en: on, of or for stairs
ex: the stair carpet
楼梯地毯

zh: （建筑物内的）楼梯
en: a set of stairs inside a building including the banisters (= posts and bars that are fixed at the side)
ex: a marble/stone/wooden staircase
大理石／石头／木楼梯

zh: 座椅式升降器（供无法步行上下楼的人使用）
en: a piece of equipment in the form of a seat that somebody can sit on to be moved up and down stairs, used by people who find it difficult to walk up and down stairs without help, especially in their own home

zh: （建筑物内或外的）楼梯，阶梯
en: a set of stairs inside or outside a building

zh: 楼梯井（建筑物内楼梯占用的空间）
en: the space in a building in which the stairs are built

zh: 股本；股份
（在公司、计划等中的）重大利益，重大利害关系
赌注
桩；标桩；篱笆桩
en: money that somebody invests in a company
ex: a 20 per cent stake in the business
持有公司20％的股份

zh: 清楚地界定自认为属于自己的东西
明确阐述自己的看法（或立场等）
监视
en: to clearly mark the limits of something that you claim is yours
ex: The president staked out his position on the issue.
总统明确阐述了他在这个问题上的立场。

zh: 警察监视
en: a situation in which police watch a building secretly to find evidence of illegal activities
ex: an armed stake-out of the building
建筑物的武装放样

zh: （某组织、工程、体系等的）参与人，参与方；有权益关系者
赌金保管人
en: a person or company that is involved in a particular organization, project, system, etc., especially because they have invested money in it
ex: All our employees are stakeholders in the company.
我们所有的员工都是公司的利益共享人。
